items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 10:1
items.html: (To the question) Every lower one is discerned as being from above downward toward its upper one, and it clothes upon the body of the upper one. And there is a difference between the Partzufim of AK and the Partzufim of the GAR of Atzilut, on the one hand, and the Partzufim of ZON of Atzilut, on the other. For in AK and in the GAR, each one holds onto all the ten Sefirot of the head of its upper one, and therefore clothes the whole body of its upper one, from its mouth and below. But ZON do not hold onto all the ten Sefirot of the head of Aba and Ima, but only onto the NHY of the head of Aba and Ima alone, for in the KHB HGT of Aba and Ima they have no share, for there is the aspect of concealed Hassadim, as said at length above, Part 1, Page 667, Answer 176. Therefore the aspect of from above downward of Aba and Ima, which ZON clothe, does not clothe the whole body of Aba and Ima, but only from the chest and below — namely, to the same extent that it holds onto the heads of Aba and Ima, so does it clothe in their body. Hence the lower third of the Tifferet of Ima is the aspect of the Keter of ZA. See there in the above-mentioned answer, where this is explained at length. (Item 6).
